module: GE extension `core_trailerRespawn`: remembers which vehicles tow which trailer (registry `trailerReg`) from coupling events, and repositions the trailer behind the towing vehicle when the latter is reset or reactivated. Depends on core_vehicles (vehsCouplerOffset, vehsCouplerTags, couplerTagsOptions) and on spawn.placeTrailer. Useful to query the composition of a road train (getVehicleTrain, getVehicleTrainHead).
notes: trailerReg[towVehicleId] = {trailerId, trailerNode, node}: a vehicle can only tow one trailer in this registry. Couplings with a 'Prop' type vehicle are ignored; coupling loops are refused.
A vehicle's type ('Trailer', 'Prop', ...) comes from the aggregates.Type field of its config, otherwise from the model's Type (getConfigType).

setEnabled(false) replaces M.onCouplerAttached and M.onCouplerDetached with `nop`: the registry is then no longer updated (the engine calls the hooks through the M table, so the change is taken into account). onVehicleResetted/onVehicleActiveChanged keep acting on the existing registry. Inconsistency: the setEnabled parameter shadows the module's local variable `enabled`, which is therefore never updated by setEnabled; getEnabled() returns the value restored by resetData/onDeserialized (true initially), not the last requested state.
onVehicleResetted is marked in the code 'TODO: Remove this when trailer respawn is disabled': core_vehicles contains a commented-out version of the same mechanism.
In multiplayer (multiplayer_vehicleSync), repositioning on reset is disabled and the trailers' active state is delegated to multiplayer_vehicleSync.requestTrailerActiveFollow.

debugEnabled.desc: false by default; the debug display of coupling nodes (debugUpdate) is not hooked up (M.onPreRender is commented out).

onSerialize.desc: Hook: saves the registry and the enabled state before a Lua reload.

onDeserialized.desc: Hook: restores the registry and reapplies setEnabled.

resetData.desc: Clears the trailer registry and re-enables the system.

getTrailerData.desc: Returns the internal registry trailerReg (not a copy).

returns.type: table<integer, {trailerId: integer, trailerNode: integer, node: integer}>

getPreviousAttachedVehicleId.desc: Returns the vehicle that tows vehId (the one whose registered trailer is vehId).

returns.desc: tow vehicle identifier, nil if there is none

getVehicleTrainHead.desc: Walks up the coupling chain to the first vehicle (head of the train).

returns.desc: train head identifier (vehId itself if it is not towed)

getVehicleTrain.desc: Returns all vehicles connected to vehId, forward and backward.

forward.desc: true: only toward the tow vehicle; false: only toward the trailers; nil: both

getConfigType.desc: Returns a vehicle's type ('Car', 'Trailer', 'Prop'...), from its config (aggregates.Type) or, failing that, its model's Type.

getAttachedNonTrailer.desc: Walks up the couplings to find the non-trailer vehicle that tows the chain containing vehId.

returns.desc: identifier of the first non-trailer vehicle, false if the chain only contains trailers

isVehicleCoupledToTrailer.desc: Indicates whether trailerId is part of the chain towed by vehId.

returns.desc: true if connected (directly or through a chain)

placeTrailer.desc: Repositions the registered trailer of vehId behind it (spawn.placeTrailer, from coupler offsets).

coupleTrailer.desc: If the coupler tag is of type 'autoCouple' (core_vehicles.couplerTagsOptions), runs beamstate.activateAutoCoupling(tag) on the tow vehicle.

setEnabled.desc: Enables or disables coupling recording (replaces onCouplerAttached/onCouplerDetached with the empty function nop if false).

getEnabled.desc: Returns the module's `enabled` variable (see notes: not updated by setEnabled).

returns.desc: true as long as resetData/onDeserialized have not changed it

onCouplerAttached.desc: Hook: a coupling closes. Records the tow/trailer direction in trailerReg (the non-trailer tows), ignores Props and loops, then emits onTrailerAttached(objId1, objId2).

onCouplerDetached.desc: Hook: a coupling opens. Only removes the record if breakForce is 0 (voluntary detachment), with a one-frame delay (job) so as not to prevent the trailer's reset.

breakForce.desc: break force; ignored if nil or > 0

onVehicleActiveChanged.desc: Hook: a vehicle is activated/deactivated. Aligns the active state of its trailer and, on activation, repositions it behind the vehicle.

onVehicleSpawned.desc: Hook: a vehicle spawns; clears its old coupling records.

onVehicleResetted.desc: Hook: a vehicle is reset; repositions its trailer behind it (disabled in multiplayer).

onVehicleDestroyed.desc: Hook: a vehicle is destroyed; clears its coupling records.
